questions.q: What is the real, honest tension this lesson describes?
options: CI/CD culture wants fast, frequent deployments, while Change Enablement wants careful review before production
ServiceNow DevOps cannot work with any external pipeline tool
ATF tests and Change Requests are mutually exclusive features
There is no real tension; CI/CD and Change Enablement always agree
questions.explain: Both instincts are legitimate — speed genuinely reduces some risks, and review genuinely catches others.

questions.q: Why does blanket fast-tracking every pipeline deployment fail as a resolution?
options: It misses the rare change that's small in code but large in business consequence, which Change Enablement exists to catch
It makes every deployment take longer than manual Change Requests
It is technically impossible to configure in ServiceNow
It eliminates the need for ATF testing entirely
questions.explain: Automatically approving everything throws away exactly the protection Change Enablement is designed to provide.

questions.q: Why does blanket gatekeeping — full CAB review for every pipeline-driven change — also fail?
options: It chokes routine, low-risk fixes with a multi-day approval cycle, defeating the point of CI/CD
It is more risky than fast-tracking everything
CAB review cannot legally apply to pipeline-driven changes
It removes ATF coverage from the pipeline
questions.explain: Requiring full review for every single change, regardless of actual risk, throws away what CI/CD is meant to deliver.

questions.q: What is the real resolution pattern mature ServiceNow DevOps implementations use?
options: Risk-based differentiation — routing low-risk, well-tested changes through pre-approved Standard Change templates, while risky changes still get full CAB review
Removing Change Enablement entirely once CI/CD is adopted
Requiring every change to go through exactly the same approval path, regardless of risk
Disabling ATF once a pipeline is connected to ServiceNow DevOps
questions.explain: This is risk-based differentiation: using actual assessed risk, not a blanket rule in either direction.

questions.q: Why can a change with passing ATF tests still deserve full CAB review rather than a Standard Change template?
options: Because passing tests prove technical correctness against what was tested, not that the change is low-risk to the business — e.g. a change to core approval logic
Because ATF tests are always unreliable and should be ignored
Because Standard Change templates are never allowed for any pipeline-driven change
Because CAB review is required for every change regardless of test results, with no exceptions
questions.explain: Test coverage and business risk are related but distinct measurements — a well-tested change can still carry high business consequence.
